## Definitions

- [fact] Verify an index ordering with explain('executionStats'). A SORT stage in the winning plan means an in-memory sort. Compare keys and documents examined against documents returned. Use cursor.hint() to force a candidate index while testing. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-rule/ · keywords: ESR rule, compound index, index, query planner, sort direction, Compound Indexes and ESR Rule
- [passage] Index prefixes are the beginning subsets of indexed fields. Compound indexes support queries on all fields included in the index prefix. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#index-prefixes · keywords: compound index, index, index key, index prefix
- [fact] Diagnose with explain('executionStats'): a combined range in indexBounds on the array path means bounds were intersected. A single open-ended bound plus a FETCH filter, or keysExamined far above nReturned, means they were not. multiKeyPaths shows which path prefixes make the index multikey. In Pachot's demo, the no-$elemMatch query examined 44 keys with a FETCH filter; with $elemMatch it examined 38 with a single combined range. — https://dev.to/franckpachot/elemmatch-and-multi-key-indexes-i6e · keywords: $elemMatch, index, multikey index, query planner, Multikey Indexes and Array Query Bounds
- [passage] - The query does not return the array field (meaning the array is not included in the query projection). This means that to cover a query, the multikey index must be [compound.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md#std-label-compound_multikey_indexes) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md#covered-queries · keywords: covered query, index, multikey index
- [passage] Since `{ a : 1 }` is a prefix of `{ a : 1, b : 1 }`, Performance Advisor suggests only `{ a : 1, b : 1 }`. To learn more about index prefixes, see [Prefixes.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-compound/#prefixes) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/index-ranking.md#index-de-duplication · keywords: compound index, index, index prefix, { a : 1 }, { a : 1, b : 1 }
- [passage] For a compound index where the index prefix keys are not strings, arrays, and embedded documents, an operation that specifies a different collation can still use the index to support comparisons on the index prefix keys. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndex.md#create-indexes-with-collation · keywords: compound index, index, index prefix
- [fact] Partial indexes with an $or filter are a known planner weak spot: forum reports (MongoDB 6.0.4 and 6.0.13) show a query repeating the identical $or still got COLLSCAN or another index, while a query with plain conditions (e.g. comments:{$exists:true}) used it. No accepted fix is shown on the threads. — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/partial-index-not-covering-or-query-filter/220425 · keywords: index, partial index, query planner, Partial Indexes
- [passage] The query does not return the array field (meaning the array is not included in the query projection). This means that to cover a query, the multikey index must be compound. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/ · keywords: index, multikey index
- [passage] Since { a : 1 } is a prefix of { a : 1, b : 1 }, Performance Advisor suggests only { a : 1, b : 1 }. To learn more about index prefixes, see Prefixes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/index-ranking/ · keywords: index, index prefix
- [passage] Not all index types can cover queries. For details on covered index support, refer to the documentation page for the corresponding index type. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ · keywords: covered query, index
- [passage] Index `{ item: 1, price: 1 }` is a [partial index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md#std-label-index-type-partial) and only indexes documents with `price` field greater than or equal to `Decimal128("10")`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/planCacheStats.md#mongodb-shell · keywords: index, partial index, { item: 1, price: 1 }, price, Decimal128("10")
- [passage] Query selectivity refers to how well the query predicate filters out documents in a collection. Query selectivity determines whether queries can use indexes effectively. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ · keywords: index, index selectivity · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md
- [passage] The document with `_id` equal to `3` is the only document that matched the [`$elemMatch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/elemmatch.md#mongodb-projection-proj.-elemMatch) criteria. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/elemMatch.md#elemmatch-https-www-mongodb-com-docs-manual-reference-operator-projection-elemmatch-md-mongodb-projection-proj-elemmatch-with-multiple-fields · keywords: $elemMatch, _id,  is the only document that matched the [

## Structure and components

- [passage] If the sort keys correspond to the index keys or an index *prefix*, MongoDB can use the index to sort the query results. A *prefix* of a compound index is a subset that consists of one or more keys at the start of the index key pattern. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes.md#sort-and-index-prefix · keywords: compound index, index, index key, index prefix · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes/
- [passage] The order of the indexed fields impacts the effectiveness of a compound index. Compound indexes contain references to documents according to the order of the fields in the index. To create efficient compound indexes, follow the [ESR (Equality, Sort, Range) guideline.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md#std-label-esr-indexing-guideline) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#field-order · keywords: ESR rule, compound index, index, index key
- [passage] The preceding index is multikey because the `genres` field contains array values. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md#covered-queries · keywords: covered query, index, multikey index, genres · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/
- [passage] However, if the shard key index is a prefix of a compound index, the compound index may become a compound multikey index if one of the trailing keys (that are not part of the shard key) indexes an array. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/ · keywords: compound index, index, multikey index
- [passage] However, if the shard key index is a [prefix](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#std-label-compound-index-prefix) of a compound index, the compound index may become a compound *multikey* index if one of the trailing keys (that are not part of the shard key) indexes an array. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md#shard-keys · keywords: compound index, index, multikey index
- [passage] **Compound indexes** are indexes that contain references to multiple fields. Compound indexes improve performance for queries on exactly the fields in the index or fields in the [index prefix.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#std-label-compound-index-prefix) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound/create-compound-index.md · keywords: compound index, index, index prefix
- [passage] Compound indexes can contain different types of sparse indexes. The combination of index types determines how the compound index matches documents. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#sparse-compound-indexes · keywords: compound index, index, sparse index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md
- [passage] The preceding query uses `$elemMatch` to return documents where the `grades` array contains at least one element that matches *both* of the specified conditions. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#example-bounds-intersection · keywords: $elemMatch, index, multikey index, grades
- [passage] The preceding query uses `$elemMatch` on the `ratings` field to require that the array contains at least one *single* element that matches both conditions. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#example · keywords: $elemMatch, index, multikey index, ratings
- [passage] For each distinct value in the array, MongoDB creates a separate entry in the index, and each entry points back to the same document. As a result, a single document can have multiple entries in a multikey index. If an array contains multiple instances of the same value, the index only includes one entry for the value. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/ · keywords: covered query, index, multikey index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md
- [passage] For example, consider a query for `"item": "saccharomyces cerevisiae"` and `"stock": 60`. If the collection contains 10000 documents matching `"item": "saccharomyces cerevisiae"` and only 100 of those documents match `"stock": 60`, the query examines 10000 keys. In the `IXSCAN` stage, the query filters those keys by the `stock` field and only returns 100 results to the next stage. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#index-prefixes · keywords: index, index prefix, query planner, "item": "saccharomyces cerevisiae", "stock": 60, IXSCAN
- [passage] When an index [covers](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md#std-label-indexes-covered-queries) a query, MongoDB can both match the query conditions **and** return the results using only the index keys. MongoDB does not need to examine documents from the collection to perform any part of the query. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#covered-queries · keywords: covered query, index, index key · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] With the compound index on `department` and `description`, the query only examines **one** index key. There is only one document in the collection where `department` is `kitchen` and the `description` contains the string `green`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/limit-number-of-items-scanned-for-text-search.md#view-number-of-documents-examined · keywords: compound index, index, index key, department, description, kitchen
- [passage] The bounds of an index scan define the parts of an index to search during a query. The computation of multikey index bounds follows special rules. For details, see Multikey Index Bounds. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/ · keywords: index, multikey index, query planner
- [passage] The bounds of an index scan define the parts of an index to search during a query. The computation of multikey index bounds follows special rules. For details, see [Multikey Index Bounds.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#std-label-indexes-multikey-bounds) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md#index-bounds · keywords: index, multikey index, query planner
- [passage] [Sparse indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#std-label-index-type-sparse) only contain entries for documents that have the indexed field. These indexes skip documents that do not have the indexed field. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-properties.md#sparse-indexes · keywords: index, index key, sparse index
- [fact] A sparse index contains entries only for documents that have the indexed field, even when the value is null. Documents missing the field are skipped. A non-sparse index stores null for those documents. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md · keywords: index, index key, sparse index, Sparse Indexes
- [passage] Specifies the number of "work units" performed by the query execution stage. Query execution divides its work into small units. A "work unit" might consist of examining a single index key, fetching a single document from the collection, applying a projection to a single document, or doing a piece of internal bookkeeping. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: index, index key, query planner
- [passage] | Field | Description | Applicable Stages | | --- | --- | --- | | `docsExamined` | Specifies the number of documents scanned during the query execution stage. | `COLLSCAN`, `FETCH` | | `keysExamined` | For query execution stages that scan an index `keysExamined` is the total number of in-bounds and out-of-bounds keys that are examined in the process of the index scan. If the index scan consists of a single contiguous range of keys, only in-bounds keys need to be examined. If the index bounds consists of several key ranges, the index scan execution process may examine out-of-bounds keys in order to skip from the end of one range to the beginning of the next. | `IXSCAN` | | `numReads` | The number of documents scanned or index keys examined during the query execution stage. **New in version 5.1** | `COLLSCAN`, `IXSCAN` | | `seeks` | The number of times that we had to seek the index cursor to a new position in order to complete the index scan. | `IXSCAN` | | `usedDisk` | Whether the stage wrote to disk. **New in version 5.3** | `GROUP` | | `spills` | The number of times the stage spilled to disk. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `spilledBytes` | The total amount of data written to disk in bytes. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `spilledRecords` | The total number of individual records spilled to disk. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `spilledDataStorageSize` | The total disk space, in bytes, used by the spilled data. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `peakTrackedMemBytes` | **New in version 8.3** Maximum number of bytes of tracked memory in use by the current query operation. Documents in a time series collection must have a valid BSON date as the value for the `timeField`. | | `metaField` | Optional. The name of the field which contains metadata in each time series document. The metadata in the specified field should be data that is used to label a unique series of documents. The metadata should rarely, if ever, change The name of the specified field may not be `_id` or the same as the `timeseries.timeField`. The field can be of any data type. Although the `metaField` field is optional, using metadata can improve query optimization. For example, MongoDB automatically [creates a compound index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-secondary-index.md#std-label-timeseries-add-secondary-index) on the `metaField` and `timeField` fields for new collections. If you do not provide a value for this field, the data is bucketed solely based on time. | | `granularity` | Optional. Do not use if setting `bucketRoundingSeconds` and `bucketMaxSpanSeconds`. Possible values are `seconds` (default), `minutes`, and `hours`. Set `granularity` to the value that most closely matches the time between consecutive incoming timestamps. This improves performance by optimizing how MongoDB stores data in the collection. For more information on granularity and bucket intervals, see [Set Granularity for Time Series Data.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-granularity.md#std-label-timeseries-granularity) | | `bucketMaxSpanSeconds` | Optional. Use with `bucketRoundingSeconds` as an alternative to `granularity`. Sets the maximum time between timestamps in the same bucket. Possible values are 1-31536000. **New in version 6.3** | | `bucketRoundingSeconds` | Optional. Use with `bucketMaxSpanSeconds` as an alternative to `granularity`. Must be equal to `bucketMaxSpanSeconds`. When a document requires a new bucket, MongoDB rounds down the document's timestamp value by this interval to set the minimum time for the bucket. **New in version 6.3** | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/out.md#syntax · keywords: compound index, index, db, $out, coll, timeseries

- [passage] | Scenario | Performance insight | | --- | --- | | You run a query or aggregation without an index. | Add an index to support the operation. | | You run an aggregation pipeline that uses a [`$lookup`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/lookup.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-lookup) stage. | Embed related data to avoid the need for a `$lookup` operation. | | You run a [`$text`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/text.md#mongodb-query-op.-text) or [`$regex`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#mongodb-query-op.-regex) query. | If possible, use [MongoDB Search](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-search/) to improve performance for text search queries. | | Your database contains too many collections. | Reduce the number of collections. | | Your documents contain an array field with too many elements. | Avoid unbounded arrays. | | The data size of individual documents is too large. | Break up large documents into separate collections. | | Your collection contains too many indexes. | Review your indexes and remove any that are unnecessary. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/performance-insights.md#behavior · keywords: index, index anti-pattern, $lookup, $text, $regex

## How it works

- [statement] A third-party blog lists further exceptions: a covered query may justify range before sort when the result set is small, and a low-cardinality equality field needs careful placement. These are practitioner advice, not in the MongoDB manual. — https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-esr-rule-compound-index/markdown · keywords: ESR rule, compound index, covered query, index, index anti-pattern, index selectivity
- [passage] The fields `"ratings.scores.q1"` and `"ratings.scores.q2"` share the field path `"ratings.scores"`. In order to compound index bounds, a query must use `$elemMatch` on the common field path. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#example-elemmatch-on-diverging-field-paths · keywords: $elemMatch, compound index, index, multikey index, query planner, "ratings.scores.q1"
- [passage] Compound bounds combine bounds for multiple keys of a [compound index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#std-label-index-type-compound). Using bounds from multiple keys reduces the time it takes to process a query because MongoDB does not need to compute results for each bound individually. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#compound-bounds-for-a-multikey-index · keywords: $elemMatch, compound index, index, multikey index
- [fact] MongoDB's manual defines unnecessary indexes as three kinds: rarely used, redundant because another compound index covers them, or not used at all. Indexing every field or every query bloats the collection and hurts write performance. — https://mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/design-antipatterns/unnecessary-indexes/ · keywords: compound index, covered query, index, index anti-pattern, Index Anti-Patterns
- [fact] In explain, an index-only plan shows PROJECTION_COVERED over IXSCAN with totalDocsExamined 0. A default projection that includes _id, or a partial projection, shows FETCH then PROJECTION_SIMPLE. Projecting _id forces a fetch because the index's $recordId is not _id. — https://dev.to/franckpachot/index-only-scan-on-json-documents-with-covering-and-multi-key-indexes-in-mongodb-53h4 · keywords: covered query, index, index selectivity, query planner, Index Selectivity and Covering Queries
- [passage] Because the constraint applies to separate documents, for a unique [multikey](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md#std-label-index-type-multikey) index, a document may have array elements that result in repeating index key values as long as the index key values for that document do not duplicate those of another document. In this case, the repeated index entry is inserted into the index only once. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique.md#unique-constraint-across-separate-documents · keywords: covered query, index, index key, multikey index
- [statement] An index supports a sort on a subset of its keys only when the query has equality conditions on all prefix keys that precede the sort keys. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-rule/ · keywords: ESR rule, compound index, index, Compound Indexes and ESR Rule · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes/
- [passage] Multikey indexes can cover queries over the non-array fields if the index tracks which field or fields cause the index to be multikey. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ · keywords: index, multikey index, covered query · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md
- [passage] Bounds intersection refers to the point where multiple bounds overlap. For example, given the bounds `[ [ 3, Infinity ] ]` and `[ [ -Infinity, 6 ] ]`, the intersection of the bounds results in `[ [ 3, 6 ] ]`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#bounds-intersection-for-a-multikey-index · keywords: $elemMatch, index, multikey index, [ [ 3, Infinity ] ], [ [ -Infinity, 6 ] ], [ [ 3, 6 ] ]
- [passage] Because the query uses `$elemMatch` to join these predicates, MongoDB intersects the bounds to: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#example-bounds-intersection · keywords: $elemMatch, index, multikey index
- [passage] Because the preceding query does not use `$elemMatch`, MongoDB does not intersect the bounds. Instead, MongoDB uses either of the following bounds: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#query-without-elemmatch · keywords: $elemMatch, index, multikey index
- [passage] The following example shows how MongoDB uses compound bounds when an index includes a non-array field and multiple array fields. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#example-compound-bounds-of-non-array-field-and-multiple-array-fields · keywords: $elemMatch, index, multikey index
- [fact] Do not rely on the stage name alone to detect coverage. A forum reply reports a covered query shows plain PROJECTION on 4.0 and PROJECTION_COVERED on 5.0. totalDocsExamined 0 is the more dependable check, except when the query returns no results. — https://mongodb.com/community/forums/t/adding-the-projected-fields-to-compound-index-to-create-covered-query-doesnt-improve-performance/199267 · keywords: covered query, index, index selectivity, Index Selectivity and Covering Queries
- [fact] MongoDB intersects bounds on a multikey array field only when $elemMatch joins the predicates. Example: grades: {$elemMatch: {$gte: 90, $lte: 99}} yields bounds [[90, 99]]. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md · keywords: $elemMatch, index, multikey index, Multikey Indexes and Array Query Bounds

- [passage] | Scenario | Index Type | | --- | --- | | A human resources department often needs to look up employees by employee ID. You can create an index on the employee ID field to improve query performance. | [Single Field Index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-single.md#std-label-indexes-single-field) | | A salesperson often needs to look up client information by location. Location is stored in an embedded object with fields like `state`, `city`, and `zipcode`. You can create an index on the `location` object to improve performance for queries on that object. When you create an index on an embedded document, only queries that specify the entire embedded document use the index. Queries on a specific field within the document do not use the index. | [Single Field Index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-single.md#std-label-indexes-single-field) on an embedded document | | A grocery store manager often needs to look up inventory items by name and quantity to determine which items are low stock. You can create a single index on both the `item` and `quantity` fields to improve query performance. | [Compound Index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#std-label-index-type-compound) | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/indexes.md#use-cases · keywords: compound index, index, single-field index, state, city, zipcode
- [passage] When an index covers a query, the explain result has an `IXSCAN` stage that is **not** a descendant of a `FETCH` stage. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#covered-queries · keywords: covered query, index, query planner, IXSCAN, FETCH · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] When [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) generates index keys on a field that holds an array, [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) generates an index key for each array element. For compound indexes, [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) calculates the [cartesian product](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-cartesian-product) of the sets of keys that are generated for each field. If both sets are large, then calculating the cartesian product could cause the operation to exceed memory limits. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md#indexes · keywords: compound index, index, index key, mongod
- [passage] In a unique multikey index, a document may have array elements that result in repeating index key values as long as the index key values for that document do not duplicate those of another document. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/ · keywords: index, index key, multikey index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md
- [passage] Even though the sort is by the indexed field, if some documents in the `movies` collection do not have a `plot` field, MongoDB does **not** select the sparse index to fulfill the query in order to return complete results. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#sparse-index-on-a-collection-cannot-return-complete-results · keywords: index, index key, sparse index, movies, plot
- [fact] A multikey index stores one entry per distinct array element, each pointing to the same document. - [passage] **Index bounds** define the range of index values that MongoDB searches when using an index to fulfill a query. When you specify multiple query predicates on an indexed field, MongoDB attempts to combine the bounds for those predicates to produce an index scan with smaller bounds. Smaller index bounds result in faster queries and reduced resource use. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md · keywords: index, index key, query planner

- [passage] If you include a [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) that specifies a [sparse index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#std-label-index-type-sparse) when you perform a [`count()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.count.md#mongodb-method-cursor.count) of all documents in a collection (i.e. with an empty query predicate), the sparse index is used even if the sparse index results in an incorrect count. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#sparse-index-and-incomplete-results · keywords: index, sparse index, hint(), count()

- [passage] You can only have one clustered index in a collection because the documents can be stored in only one order. - [passage] Although indexes improve query performance, adding an index has negative performance impact for write operations. - [passage] The following example demonstrates sorting when index keys have the same or different types. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes/ · keywords: mongodb-compound-index-design
- [passage] - If there are secondary indexes for the clustered collection, the collection has a larger storage size. This is because secondary indexes on a clustered collection with large clustered index keys may have a larger storage size than secondary indexes on a non-clustered collection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections.md#limitations · keywords: mongodb-compound-index-design
- [passage] You can create indexes suggested by the Performance Advisor directly within the Performance Advisor itself. When you create indexes, keep the ratio of reads to writes on the target collection in mind. Indexes come with a performance cost, but are more than worth the cost for frequent queries on large data sets. To learn more about indexing strategies, see Indexing Strategies. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/ · keywords: mongodb-compound-index-design
- [passage] The following sections explain the index properties that you can specify when building an index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-properties.md · keywords: mongodb-compound-index-design
- [passage] When you insert data into a time series collection, the internal collection automatically organizes the data into an optimized storage format using [buckets](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing.md#std-label-timeseries-bucketing-specifics). If a suitable bucket exists, MongoDB inserts new data into that bucket. If a suitable bucket does not exist, MongoDB creates a new bucket. To optimize storage, choose a `metaField` that rarely changes to create time series collections with fewer, more densely packed buckets. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-considerations.md#storage-and-cardinality · keywords: index selectivity, metaField
- [passage] For each open bucket, the catalog maintains information such as the `metaField`, active writers, covered time span, number of documents, size, and recent operations. Because MongoDB creates separate buckets for documents with a different `metaField`, multiple buckets are typically open at the same time. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing.md#the-bucket-catalog · keywords: covered query, metaField · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-bucketing/
- [passage] The sort direction is descending because the `sortBy` value is "-1". — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sortArray.md#sort-on-a-subfield · keywords: sort direction, sortBy
- [passage] - Ensure that your schema design does not rely on indexed arrays that grow in length without bound. Typically, best performance can be achieved when such indexed arrays have fewer than 1000 elements. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/production-checklist-development.md#schema-design · keywords: multikey index
- [passage] The following sections show the output differences when you use `$elemMatch` with a single query condition, and omit `$elemMatch`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/elemMatch.md#single-query-condition · keywords: $elemMatch
- [passage] When unset, `contention` defaults to `8`, which provides high performance for most workloads. Higher contention improves the performance of insert and update operations on low cardinality fields, but decreases find performance. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/fundamentals/encrypt-and-query.md#advanced-query-parameters · keywords: index selectivity, contention
- [passage] Collections with fine-grained or changing `metaField` values generate many sparsely packed, short-lived buckets, increasing the cardinality of your collection. Increasing cardinality leads to decreased storage and query efficiency. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-considerations.md#storage-and-cardinality · keywords: index selectivity, metaField
- [passage] All time series collection use a compressed bucket format when you append data into opened or reopened buckets. Compressing time series data in the cache supports high [cardinality](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-cardinality) workloads while preserving efficient query performance. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-considerations.md#compression-and-hardware · keywords: index selectivity
- [passage] Finds the distinct values for a specified field across a single collection or view and returns the unique results in an array. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.distinct.md#definition · keywords: index selectivity
- [passage] mongos performs a broadcast operation for queries that do not include the shard key, routing queries to all shards in the cluster. Some queries that do include the shard key may still result in a broadcast operation depending on the distribution of data in the cluster and the selectivity of the query. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/ · keywords: index selectivity · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md

## How-to and procedures

- [passage] Create a [compound multikey index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#std-label-index-type-compound) on the `item` and `ratings` fields: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#example-compound-bounds-of-non-array-field-and-array-field · keywords: $elemMatch, compound index, index, multikey index, item, ratings
- [passage] Create a compound index on the `ratings.score` and the `ratings.by` fields: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#example · keywords: $elemMatch, compound index, index, multikey index, ratings.score, ratings.by
- [passage] Create a compound index on the `ratings.scores.q1` and the `ratings.scores.q2` fields: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#example-elemmatch-on-diverging-field-paths · keywords: $elemMatch, compound index, index, multikey index, ratings.scores.q1, ratings.scores.q2
- [passage] Create a unique compound [multikey](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md#std-label-index-type-multikey) index on `email` and `name`: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique.md#unique-compound-index · keywords: compound index, index, multikey index, email, name
- [passage] To compound the bounds for `"ratings.score"` with the bounds for `"ratings.by"`, the query must use `$elemMatch`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#example-compound-bounds-of-non-array-field-and-multiple-array-fields · keywords: $elemMatch, index, multikey index, "ratings.score", "ratings.by"
- [passage] To compound the bounds, the query must use `$elemMatch` on the common path `"ratings.scores"`: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#example-elemmatch-on-diverging-field-paths · keywords: $elemMatch, index, multikey index, "ratings.scores"
- [passage] To achieve a covered query, you must index projected fields. The ESR (Equality, Sort, Range) rule applies to the order of fields in the index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ · keywords: ESR rule, covered query, index
- [passage] To achieve a covered query, you must index projected fields. The [ESR (Equality, Sort, Range) rule](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md#std-label-esr-indexing-guideline) applies to the order of fields in the index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md#example · keywords: ESR rule, covered query, index
- [passage] To check if MongoDB must perform an in-memory sort, append [`cursor.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) to the query and check the [explain results](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#std-label-explain-results). If the query plan contains a `SORT` stage, then MongoDB must perform an in-memory sort operation. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#sort-and-index-use · keywords: index, query planner, sort direction, cursor.explain(), SORT · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowDiskUse/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowDiskUse.md
- [passage] To learn how MongoDB combines multikey index bounds to improve performance, see Multikey Index Bounds. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/ · keywords: index, multikey index, query planner
- [passage] To see whether your operation results in a `DISTINCT_SCAN`, check your operation's [explain results.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#std-label-explain-results) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/group.md#retrieve-distinct-values · keywords: index selectivity, query planner, DISTINCT_SCAN
- [passage] To create a `partial` index, use the [`db.collection.createIndex()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindex.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.createIndex) method with the `partialFilterExpression` option. The `partialFilterExpression` option accepts a document that specifies the filter condition using: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md#create-a-partial-index · keywords: index, partial index, partial, db.collection.createIndex(), partialFilterExpression
- [passage] To learn how to manage indexes in MongoDB Compass, see [Manage Indexes.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-indexes.md#std-label-manage-indexes) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md#create-a-partial-index · keywords: index, partial index
- [passage] To index fields in embedded documents, use [dot notation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-dot-notation). See [Create an Index on an Embedded Field.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-single/create-single-field-index.md#std-label-index-embedded-fields) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md#embedded-documents · keywords: covered query, index
- [passage] Create a compound index to support sorting on multiple fields. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes/ · keywords: compound index, index
- [passage] To improve query performance for [time series collections](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-time-series-collection), add one or more [secondary indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-secondary-index) to support common time series query patterns. Starting in MongoDB 6.3, MongoDB automatically creates a [compound index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#std-label-index-type-compound) on the `metaField` and `timeField` fields for new collections. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-secondary-index.md · keywords: compound index, index, metaField, timeField · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries-collections.md
- [passage] Create the following compound index on the `type` and `item` fields: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/meta.md#meta-indexkey · keywords: compound index, index, type, item
- [passage] Create a [compound index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#std-label-index-type-compound) to support sorting on multiple fields. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes.md#sort-on-multiple-fields · keywords: compound index, index
- [passage] To support the query, add a [compound index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#std-label-index-type-compound). With compound indexes, the order of the fields matter. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md#mongodb-shell · keywords: compound index, index
- [passage] To support the query, add a compound index. With compound indexes, the order of the fields matter. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan/ · keywords: compound index, index
- [passage] To create a compound index, use the [`db.collection.createIndex()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindex.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.createIndex) method: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound/create-compound-index.md · keywords: compound index, index, db.collection.createIndex()
- [passage] To create a compound index, see [Create a Compound Index.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound/create-compound-index.md#std-label-index-create-compound) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#get-started · keywords: compound index, index
- [passage] Create indexes for commonly issued queries. If a query searches multiple fields, create a compound index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ · keywords: compound index, index
- [passage] To determine whether a query is a covered query, use the db.collection.explain() or the explain() method. See Covered Queries. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ · keywords: covered query, query planner
- [passage] Create indexes for commonly issued queries. If a query searches multiple fields, create a [compound index.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#std-label-index-type-compound) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md#create-indexes-to-support-queries · keywords: compound index, index
- [passage] To determine whether a query is a covered query, use the [`db.collection.explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.explain) or the [`explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) method. See [Covered Queries.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#std-label-explain-output-covered-queries) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md#explain-results · keywords: covered query, query planner, db.collection.explain(), explain()
- [passage] Create a compound index on the `inventory` collection that contains the following fields: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/limit-number-of-items-scanned-for-text-search.md#procedure · keywords: compound index, index, inventory
- [passage] Ensure that equality fields always come first. Placing equality fields first keeps the remaining index fields in sorted order. Choose whether to use a sort or range field next based on your index's specific needs: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-rule/ · keywords: mongodb-compound-index-design
- [passage] Create a unique compound [multikey](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md#std-label-index-type-multikey) index on `a.loc` and `a.qty`: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique/create-compound.md#compound-unique-indexes-on-fields-with-embedded-arrays · keywords: index, multikey index, a.loc, a.qty
- [passage] To use the partial index, a query must contain the filter expression (or a modified filter expression that specifies a subset of the filter expression) as part of its query condition. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md#query-coverage · keywords: index, partial index
- [passage] Use a Sparse Index to Improve $exists Performance — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists/ · keywords: index, sparse index
- [passage] To create a sparse index, use the [`db.collection.createIndex()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindex.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.createIndex) method with the `sparse` option set to `true`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#create-a-sparse-index · keywords: index, sparse index, db.collection.createIndex(), sparse, true
- [passage] To obtain the correct count of the number of documents in the `movies` collection, do not [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) with a [sparse index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#std-label-index-type-sparse) when performing a count of all documents in a collection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#sparse-index-and-incomplete-results · keywords: index, sparse index, movies, hint()
- [passage] To use the sparse index, explicitly specify the index with [`hint()`:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#sparse-index-on-a-collection-cannot-return-complete-results · keywords: index, sparse index, hint()
- [passage] To hide an index, you must have [featureCompatibilityVersion](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setfeaturecompatibilityversion.md#std-label-view-fcv) set to `7.0` or greater. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/collMod.md#hide-an-index-from-the-query-planner · keywords: index, query planner, 7.0
- [passage] To analyze query performance, see [Interpret Explain Plan Results.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md#create-indexes-to-support-queries · keywords: index, query planner
- [passage] To improve query performance, build indexes on fields that appear often in queries and for all operations that [sort by a field.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/compass/query/sort.md#std-label-compass-query-bar-sort) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/compass/indexes.md · keywords: mongodb-compound-index-design
- [passage] Create Selective Indexes to Answer Queries Efficiently — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-rule/ · keywords: index, index selectivity · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline/
- [passage] To learn more about the impact of unnecessary indexes, see [Remove Unnecessary Indexes.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/design-antipatterns/unnecessary-indexes/) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/drop-indexes.md · keywords: index, index anti-pattern
- [passage] Add one or more indexes to better serve the inefficient queries. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/query-targeting.md#fix-the-immediate-problem · keywords: mongodb-compound-index-design
- [passage] To match scalar values, use the equality operator along with the scalar value that you want to match (`{$eq: <scalar value>}`). For example, the following [`find()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.find) operation queries for all documents where the value of the `zipcode` field is `"63109"`. The projection includes the matching element of the `athletics` array where the value is `basketball`: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/elemMatch.md#elemmatch-https-www-mongodb-com-docs-manual-reference-operator-projection-elemmatch-md-mongodb-projection-proj-elemmatch-with-multiple-fields · keywords: $elemMatch, {$eq: <scalar value>}, find(), zipcode, "63109", athletics
- [passage] To avoid an in-memory sort, place the range filter after the sort predicate. For more information on in-memory sorts, see cursor.allowDiskUse(). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-rule/ · keywords: sort direction · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline/
- [passage] To avoid an in-memory sort, place the range filter after the sort predicate. For more information on in-memory sorts, see [`cursor.allowDiskUse()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowdiskuse.md#mongodb-method-cursor.allowDiskUse) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md#range · keywords: sort direction, cursor.allowDiskUse()
- [passage] To specify criteria on multiple fields of documents inside that array, use the [`$elemMatch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/elemmatch.md#mongodb-query-op.-elemMatch) query operator. The following query returns the first document inside a `grades` array that has a `mean` of greater than 70 and a `grade` of greater than 90. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/positional.md#array-field-limitations · keywords: $elemMatch, grades, mean, grade
- [passage] To perform an `$elemMatch` projection when using the .NET/C# driver, call the `ElemMatch()` method on the projection builder. Pass the name of the array field to project and the filter to apply to the array elements. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/elemMatch.md#zipcode-search · keywords: $elemMatch, ElemMatch()
- [passage] To perform an `$elemMatch` operation against scalar values in an array when using the .NET/C# driver, call the `ElemMatch()` method on the projection builder. Pass the name of the array field to project and an equality filter for the field `"$eq"` and the value you want to compare against. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/elemMatch.md#elemmatch-https-www-mongodb-com-docs-manual-reference-operator-projection-elemmatch-md-mongodb-projection-proj-elemmatch-with-multiple-fields · keywords: $elemMatch, ElemMatch(), "$eq"
- [passage] To find the distinct values for a sharded collection, use the aggregation pipeline with the [`$group`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/group.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-group) stage instead. See [Distinct Operation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions-operations.md#std-label-transactions-operations-distinct) for details. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.distinct.md#transactions · keywords: index selectivity, $group · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/distinct.md
- [passage] To find the distinct values for a sharded collection, use the aggregation pipeline with the $group stage instead. See Distinct Operation for details. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/distinct/ · keywords: index selectivity
- [passage] To filter documents based on elements in an array field, use the [`$elemMatch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/elemmatch.md#mongodb-query-op.-elemMatch) operator in the query predicate of the `$match` stage: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/match.md#match-array-elements · keywords: $elemMatch, $match
- [passage] Use the [`$elemMatch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/elemmatch.md#mongodb-query-op.-elemMatch) operator to specify multiple criteria on array elements so that at least one array element satisfies all the specified criteria. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-arrays.md#query-for-an-array-element-that-meets-multiple-criteria · keywords: $elemMatch · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-array-of-documents.md

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Covered indexes cost size. In a forum case a fully covering index was about 8x the single-field index and ran slightly slower than it for a name-only query. Unanchored regex scans the whole index keyspace; an anchored prefix regex bounds the scan and is much faster. — https://mongodb.com/community/forums/t/adding-the-projected-fields-to-compound-index-to-create-covered-query-doesnt-improve-performance/199267 · keywords: covered query, index, index anti-pattern, index selectivity, single-field index, Index Selectivity and Covering Queries
- [statement] Real-world symptom: on MongoDB 4.4.14 a range query on a multikey path (products.productInfo.productId) with $gt and $lte used only the (479894, inf] bound, with the $lte as a FETCH filter. It examined 741,071 keys and 399,367 docs and took 10-14 s. Wrapping both predicates in $elemMatch fixed it. — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/mongo-indexbounds-doubts/165994 · keywords: $elemMatch, index, multikey index, query planner, Multikey Indexes and Array Query Bounds
- [passage] For any configuration of granularity parameters, the maximum size of a bucket is 1000 measurements or 125KB of data, whichever is lower. MongoDB may also enforce a lower maximum size for high cardinality data with many unique values, so that the working set of buckets fits within the [WiredTiger cache.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/wiredtiger.md#std-label-storage-wiredtiger) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-limitations.md#bucket-size · keywords: index selectivity

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [fact] Multikey indexes can cover queries over non-array fields only if the index tracks which fields cause it to be multikey. They cannot cover queries over array fields. In one forum case an index including an array field forced a FETCH and examined about 5.1M documents; the same index without that field examined none. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ · keywords: index, index anti-pattern, index selectivity, multikey index, query planner, Index Selectivity and Covering Queries
- [statement] Diagnostic workflow: run explain('executionStats') or explain('allPlansExecution') and look for AND_SORTED/AND_HASH in the winning or rejected plans; use $indexStats to compare per-index usage. Intersection is a fallback when a compound index cannot be added. — https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-how-to-use-index-intersection-in-mongodb/markdown · keywords: compound index, index, index intersection, query planner, Index Intersection
- [passage] If your query specifies `$elemMatch` on fields that diverge from a common path, MongoDB **cannot** compound the bounds of index keys from the same array. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#example-elemmatch-on-diverging-field-paths · keywords: $elemMatch, index, index key, multikey index
- [passage] MongoDB cannot compound the index bounds and the `"ratings.scores.q2"` field is unconstrained during the index scan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#example-elemmatch-on-diverging-field-paths · keywords: $elemMatch, index, multikey index, query planner, "ratings.scores.q2"
- [fact] With .sort(), an $in list of fewer than 201 elements is expanded and merged in index sort order with a SORT_MERGE stage, so it acts like an equality field. At 201 or more elements it is ordered like a range, and later index fields cannot be used for sorting. MongoDB says this threshold is not guaranteed to stay the same across versions. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-rule/ · keywords: ESR rule, compound index, index, Compound Indexes and ESR Rule
- [passage] If the query does not join the conditions on the array field with `$elemMatch`, MongoDB cannot intersect the multikey index bounds. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#query-without-elemmatch · keywords: $elemMatch, index, multikey index, query planner
- [passage] [Multikey indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md#std-label-index-type-multikey) cannot cover queries over array fields. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md#indexes · keywords: index, multikey index, covered query · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md
- [passage] If MongoDB cannot compound the two bounds, MongoDB constrains the index scan by the bound on the leading field. In this example, the leading field is `temperature`, resulting in a constraint of `temperature: [ [ 80, Infinity ] ]`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md#compound-bounds-for-a-multikey-index · keywords: $elemMatch, index, multikey index, temperature, temperature: [ [ 80, Infinity ] ]
- [passage] However, the following query cannot use the partial index on the `name` field because using the index results in an incomplete result set. Specifically, the query predicate includes the condition `password: { $exists: false }` while the index has the filter `password: { $exists: true }`. That is, the query `{ name: "Ned Stark", password: { $exists: false } }` matches more documents (users without passwords) than the index covers. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md#query-coverage · keywords: covered query, index, partial index, name, password: { $exists: false }, password: { $exists: true }
- [fact] MongoDB docs recommend a partial index over a sparse index for precise control. A partial index with partialFilterExpression {field:{$exists:true}} reproduces sparse behavior, and a single index cannot specify both partialFilterExpression and sparse. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md · keywords: index, partial index, sparse index, Sparse Indexes
- [statement] From MongoDB 9.0, a query on an indexed field that becomes multikey while the query runs may fail with QueryKilledError; re-run it after the insert or update finishes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md · keywords: index, index key, multikey index, Multikey Indexes and Array Query Bounds
- [passage] When a query specifies an exact match for an array as a whole, MongoDB uses the multikey index to locate documents that contain the first element of that array. However, it cannot match the entire array using the index alone. MongoDB then fetches the candidate documents and filters them to return only those whose array exactly matches the query array. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/ · keywords: index, multikey index, query planner · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md
- [passage] The above unsupported index types are ignored by the query planner in strict mode. For example, attempting to use a sparse index with cursor.hint() results in the following BadValue error: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/ · keywords: index, query planner, sparse index
- [passage] - You cannot specify both the `partialFilterExpression` option and the `sparse` option. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md#restrictions · keywords: partial index, sparse index, partialFilterExpression, sparse
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 7.3, you cannot create equivalent indexes, which are partial indexes with the same index keys and the same partial expressions that use a [collation.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md#equivalent-indexes · keywords: index, index key, partial index
- [passage] - The above unsupported index types are ignored by the [query planner](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-query-plans-query-optimization) in [strict mode](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/stable-api.md#std-label-stable-api-strict-client). For example, attempting to use a `sparse` index with [`cursor.hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) results in the following `BadValue` error: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndexes.md#stable-api · keywords: index, query planner, sparse index, sparse, cursor.hint(), BadValue · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md
- [passage] | `$exists` Query | Using a Sparse Index | Using a Non-Sparse Index | | --- | --- | --- | | `{ $exists: true }` | Most efficient. MongoDB can make an exact match and does not require a `FETCH`. | More efficient than queries without an index, but still requires a `FETCH`. | | `{ $exists: false }` | Cannot use the index and requires a `COLLSCAN`. | Requires a `FETCH`. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists.md#use-a-sparse-index-to-improve-exists-performance · keywords: index, query planner, sparse index, $exists, { $exists: true }, FETCH
- [passage] | Field | Description | | --- | --- | | [into](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-into) | The output collection. Specify either: The collection name as a string to output to a collection in the same database where the aggregation is run. For example:`into: "myOutput"`; The database and collection name in a document to output to a collection in the specified database. For example:`into: { db:"myDB", coll:"myOutput" }` If the output collection does not exist, `$merge` creates the collection: For a [replica set](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/replication.md#std-label-replica-set) or a standalone, if the output database does not exist, `$merge` also creates the database.; For a [sharded cluster](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/sharding.md#std-label-sharded-cluster), the specified output database must already exist. The output collection can be a sharded collection. | | [on](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-on) | Optional. Field or fields that act as a unique identifier for a document. The identifier determines if a results document [matches](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenMatched) an existing document in the output collection. Specify either: A single field name as a string. For example:`on: "_id"`; A combination of fields in an array. For example:`on: [ "date", "customerId" ]`The order of the fields in the array does not matter, and you cannot specify the same field multiple times. For the specified field or fields: The aggregation results documents must contain the field(s) specified in the `on`, unless the `on` field is the `_id` field. If the `_id` field is missing from a results document, MongoDB adds it automatically.; For deployments running MongoDB 8.0 and earlier, specified field or fields for `on` cannot be missing or contain a null value. Starting in MongoDB 8.1, if the [supporting index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-on-supporting-index) is not sparse, the specified field or fields for `on` can be missing or contain a null value.; The specified field or fields cannot contain an array value. `$merge` requires a [unique](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique.md#std-label-index-type-unique) index with keys that correspond to the [on](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-on) identifier fields. Although the order of the index key specification does not matter, the unique index must only contain the `on` fields as its keys. The index must also have the same [collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) as the aggregation's collation.; The unique index can be a [sparse](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#std-label-index-type-sparse) index.; The unique index cannot be a [partial](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md#std-label-index-type-partial) index.; For output collections that already exist, the corresponding index must already exist. The default value for [on](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-on) depends on the output collection: If the output collection does not exist, the [on](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-on) identifier must be and defaults to the `_id` field. The corresponding unique `_id` index is automatically created.To use a different [on](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-on) identifier field(s) for a collection that does not exist, you can create the collection first by creating a unique index on the desired field(s). See the [section on non-existent output collection](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-use-different-on) for an example.; Starting in MongoDB 8.3, the server checks to ensure that the automatically created `_id` index matches the query's collation. If the collations do not match, the `_id` index cannot provide uniqueness for the query, and the query will not run.; If the existing output collection is unsharded, the `on` identifier defaults to the `_id` field.; If the existing output collection is a sharded collection, the [on](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-on) identifier defaults to all the shard key fields and the `_id` field. If specifying a different `on` identifier, the `on` must contain all the shard key fields. | | [whenMatched](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenMatched) | Optional. The behavior of `$merge` if a result document and an existing document in the collection have the same value for the specified [on](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-on) field(s). You can specify either: One of the pre-defined action strings:["replace":](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenMatched-replace)Replace the existing document in the [output collection](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-into) with the matching results document.When performing a replace, the replacement document cannot result in a modification of the `_id` value or, if the output collection is sharded, the shard key value. Otherwise, the operation generates an error.To avoid this error, if the [on](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-on) field does not include the `_id` field, remove the `_id` field in the aggregation results to avoid the error, such as with a preceding [`$unset`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unset.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-unset) stage, and so on.; ["keepExisting":](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenMatched-keepExisting)Keep the existing document in the [output collection.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-into); ["merge"](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenMatched-merge) (Default):Merge the matching documents (similar to the [`$mergeObjects`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/expression/mergeobjects.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-mergeObjects) operator).If the results document contains fields not in the existing document, add these new fields to the existing document.; If the results document contains fields in the existing document, replace the existing field values with those from the results document.For example, if the output collection has the document:`{ _id: 1, a: 1, b: 1 }`And the aggregation results has the document:`{ _id: 1, b: 5, z: 1 }`Then, the merged document is:`{ _id: 1, a: 1, b: 5, z: 1 }`When performing a merge, the merged document cannot result in a modification of the `_id` value or, if the output collection is sharded, the shard key value. Otherwise, the operation generates an error.To avoid this error, if the [on](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-on) field does not include the `_id` field, remove the `_id` field in the aggregation results to avoid the error, such as with a preceding [`$unset`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unset.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-unset) stage, and so on.; ["fail":](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenMatched-fail)Stop and fail the aggregation operation. Any changes to the output collection from previous documents are not reverted.; An aggregation pipeline to update the document in the collection.`[ <stage1>, <stage2> ... ]`The pipeline can only consist of the following stages:[`$addFields`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/addfields.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-addFields) and its alias [`$set`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/set.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-set); [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) and its alias [`$unset`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unset.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-unset); [`$replaceRoot`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/replaceroot.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-replaceRoot) and its alias [`$replaceWith`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/replacewith.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-replaceWith)The pipeline cannot modify the [on](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-on) field's value. For example, if you are matching on the field `month`, the pipeline cannot modify the `month` field.The whenMatched `pipeline` can directly access the fields of the existing documents in the **output** collection using `$<field>`.To access the fields from the aggregation results documents, use either:The built-in `$$new` variable to access the field. Specifically, `$$new.<field>`. The `$$new` variable is only available if the [let](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-let) specification is omitted.; The user-defined variables in the [let](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-let) field.Specify the double dollar sign ($$) prefix together with the variable name in the form `$$<variable_name>`. For example, `$$year`. If the variable is set to a document, you can also include a document field in the form `$$<variable_name>.<field>`. For example, `$$year.month`.For more examples, see [Use Variables to Customize the Merge.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-variables-example) | | [let](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-let) | Optional. Specifies variables for use in the [whenMatched pipeline.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenMatched-pipeline) Specify a document with the variable names and value expressions: `{ <variable_name_1>: <expression_1>, ..., <variable_name_n>: <expression_n> }` If unspecified, defaults to `{ new: "$$ROOT" }` (see [`ROOT`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/aggregation-variables.md#mongodb-variable-variable.ROOT)). The [whenMatched pipeline](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenMatched-pipeline) can access the `$$new` variable. To access the variables in the [whenMatched pipeline:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenMatched-pipeline) Specify the double dollar sign ($$) prefix together with the variable name in the form `$$<variable_name>`. For example, `$$year`. If the variable is set to a document, you can also include a document field in the form `$$<variable_name>.<field>`. For example, `$$year.month`. For examples, see [Use Variables to Customize the Merge.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-variables-example) | | [whenNotMatched](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenNotMatched) | Optional. The behavior of `$merge` if a result document does not match an existing document in the out collection. You can specify one of the pre-defined action strings: ["insert"](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenNotMatched-insert) (Default):Insert the document into the output collection.; ["discard":](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenNotMatched-discard)Discard the document. Specifically, `$merge` does not insert the document into the output collection.; ["fail":](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenNotMatched-fail)Stop and fail the aggregation operation. Any changes already written to the output collection are not reverted. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#syntax · keywords: index, index key, sparse index, into: "myOutput", into: { db:"myDB", coll:"myOutput" }, $merge
- [passage] If MongoDB cannot use an index or indexes to obtain the sort order, the results include a `SORT` stage indicating an in-memory sort operation. If the explain plan does not contain an explicit `SORT` stage, then MongoDB used an index to obtain the sort order. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#sort-stage · keywords: index, query planner, sort direction, SORT · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [fact] A compound multikey index allows at most one array-valued field per document. Creating the index fails if documents have arrays in more than one indexed field, and later inserts that violate this fail. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md · keywords: index, index key, multikey index, Multikey Indexes and Array Query Bounds
- [fact] From MongoDB 7.3, equivalent indexes (same keys and same partial expression with a collation) cannot be created; pre-existing ones in upgraded databases are kept but only the first is used. Since 5.0, multiple partial indexes with the same key pattern are allowed if filters are not equivalent. — https://mongodb.com/docs/v7.3/core/index-partial · keywords: index, index key, partial index, Partial Indexes
